{{Short description|31st season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=May 2019}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1961–62 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 15 October 1961 – 6 May 1962 |teams = 20 |team1 = |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles = |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |two = Kerry |previous = [[1960–61 National Hurling League|1960–61]] |next = [[1962–63 National Hurling League|1962–63]] }} The '''1961–62 National Hurling League''' was the 31st season of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |image = |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1961-62 |winners=[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]
2nd National League title
Captain: [[Alfie Hickey]] |relegated= |continentalcup1= |continentalcup1 qualifiers= |continentalcup2= |continentalcup2 qualifiers= |league topscorer=[[File: Colours of Cork.svg|border|20px]] [[Christy Ring]] (13-18) |best goalkeeper= |biggest home win= |biggest away win= |highest scoring= |matches= 28 |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1960-61 National Hurling League|1960-61]] |nextseason=[[1962-63 National Hurling League|1962-63]] |updated=26 February 2017 }} The league saw a major restructuring for the 1961–62 season. Division 1 was split into Group 1A and Group 1B consisting of five teams each and Group 1C consisting of four teams. The top team in each group qualified for the knock-out stage. [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1960-61 National Hurling League|1960-61 season]]. [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] and [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] entered Division 1 as part of the restructuring. On 6 May 1962, [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] won the title after a 1–16 to 1–8 win over [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the final.
